header:
Date: 2028-02-20 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sara Ahmed (Nova Fintech - Head of ML), Dmitri Pavlov (Nova - Infra), Priya Rao (Nova - CTO)
summary: Discovery focused on integration options for Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Customer evaluating SDK patterns (direct SDK vs gateway/proxy), LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility, rate limit behavior, and observability hooks. Security and data residency (VPC, KMS, SOC2) are gating criteria. Agreed next steps: share pricing/security docs, sample LangChain/LlamaIndex notebooks, and schedule infra deep-dive to run benchmarks.
topics: Rate limits and quotas (per-route vs global)
Observability hooks: traces, token-level cost, dashboards
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, data residency, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood. quick intros?
[00:10] Sara: hi, sara here, head of ml, we own the model infra and production prompts.
[00:15] Dmitri: dmitri, infra eng, i'll be the one running the benchmarks and looking at networking/VPC stuff.
[00:22] Marcus: marcus li, solutions engineer, i'll cover integration patterns and performance.
[00:28] Priya: priya, cto, tuning in for security and ops questions.
[00:35] Lena: great. the goal today is to understand how you want to integrate \u0014 are you thinking direct sdk calls from services, or a gateway/proxy approach? also to surface constraints like rate limits, seq lengths, and security needs.
[00:50] Sara: we're prototyping in python. most of our stack uses langchain and llamaindex, so we need examples that fit that. latency matters for some flows, but cost matters too, so we may want batching or dedicate capacity.
[01:10] Marcus: yeah, we have SDKs in python/node and first-class examples for langchain and llamaindex. for LangChain we typically show the chain-of-thought plus retriever pattern. some customers run directly via the sdk from app servers, others put a sidecar/gateway to centralize rate limits and token caching.
[01:35] Dmitri: can you explain the gateway pattern? we are sensitive about API keys in app hosts.
[01:42] Marcus: sure \u0014 a gateway is basically an authenticated proxy that owns the long-lived credentials. Calls from your app go to the gateway which applies per-route quotas, batching, and can reuse prefix/K-V cache, so you reduce tokens. it's also useful for routing to dedicated pools vs hosted.
[02:05] Priya: so that handles kv cache? we do a lot of retrieval-augmented generation, so prefix hits are key. i heard you say K-V cash earlier in docs, i wanted to confirm it's KV cache.
[02:16] Marcus: yes kv cache \u0014 apologies, sometimes the auto-transcripts say K-V cash. our runtime supports prefix/KV caching and will reuse kvcache across similar prompts to save tokens.
[02:30] Sara: on the langchain side, do you provide connectors or do we have to write an adapter?
[02:36] Marcus: we provide an official python sdk that implements the OpenAI API surface plus a Redwood client. we also have curated langchain examples and an LlamaIndex connector that works with the retriever API. the sample notebooks will be in the repo we share.
[02:55] Sara: perfect. what about rate limits \u0014 we have spikes up to 120 RPS for some endpoints.
[03:02] Marcus: we expose both per-key and per-route quotas; for hosted tiers there's default soft limits and you can request raise; for dedicated we do capacity planning and can guarantee throughput. the gateway pattern helps smooth spikes via batching and queueing.
[03:20] Dmitri: do you support token-level billing breakdowns? product needs to understand cost per feature.
[03:25] Lena: yes \u0014 in the console we have token-level cost & latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and export hooks for ingestion into datadog or prometheus. also trace ids to connect request traces to your trace system.
[03:44] Priya: how do observability hooks work? we prefer webhooks + open telemetry traces.
[03:50] Marcus: we emit request metrics and offer an open telemetry exporter; you can also push traces and token-level spans. audit logs and request bodies are available in private deployments or with appropriate retention controls in hosted. we also have webhooks for async job completions.
[04:10] Sara: security \u0014 we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS. can dedicated or private meet our requirements?
[04:17] Lena: yes. we are SOC 2 compliant for hosted. Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and stricter network controls. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the control plane in your environment and integrates with your KMS/HSM and SAML SSO; audit logging is built-in.
[04:36] Dmitri: what about data residency? some EU customers require data to stay in region.
[04:41] Lena: we support region pinning and can provision dedicated capacity in specific regions; private on-prem solves that fully.
[04:50] Sara: latency \u0014 for inference on 2k token sequences we need 200-400ms p95 ideally, is that feasible?
[04:58] Marcus: depends on model and quantization; with our optimized runtime and serving kernels you can get low latency on shorter seq. for 2k it's heavier \u0014 we can use batching strategies and quantized variants. we should run a spike test with your traffic patterns.
[05:15] Priya: can you do rollouts/canarying? we want to test model changes gradually.
[05:20] Marcus: yes, rollouts are first-class: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous model variant if latency or quality regresses. you can pin versions per-route.
[05:33] Dmitri: how do you authenticate? do you issue short-lived keys for the gateway?
[05:38] Marcus: typical patterns: short-lived tokens from your auth service, mutual TLS between gateway and our endpoints, or for private deployments you operate your own control plane and integrate with your identity provider via SAML.
[05:50] Sara: what's the onboarding timeline for dedicated vs private?
[05:55] Lena: hosted = minutes to hours. dedicated = a few weeks for capacity provisioning and testing. private on-prem = months typically due to install, networking, and security reviews.
[06:10] Priya: cost \u0014 can you give rough deltas?
[06:13] Lena: rough: hosted is pay-as-you-go; dedicated is committed capacity so lower unit cost but commit; private has higher fixed cost but full control and lower per-token at scale. i'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[06:28] Sara: ok. for the sample integration, can you include both sdk direct call example and gateway proxy example?
[06:34] Marcus: absolutely, we'll include both patterns and a small benchmark harness.
[06:40] Sasha: [misattributed speaker noise] uh yeah
[06:44] Lena: (laugh) auto-transcript error \u0014 ignore.
[06:48] Dmitri: on observability, do you keep request bodies in audit logs by default? we need PII controls.
[06:55] Marcus: by default hosted redwood redacts sensitive fields and provides configurable retention; for enterprise dedicated/private you can configure full retention and integrate with your S3 or SIEM for long-term archive.
[07:12] Sara: about langchain: does the rehtraining/embeddings flow fit? we use embeddings heavily for retrieval.
[07:19] Marcus: embeddings are first-class. we provide batch embedding endpoints and off-the-shelf semantic search examples that plug into LlamaIndex. we also support vector DB exports and retriever connectors.
[07:35] Priya: is there an internal gateway we must use, or can our existing api-gateway call redwood directly?
[07:41] Marcus: you can do either. many teams layer Redwood behind their existing gateway to centralize auth and routing; others call directly from app services to reduce latency. it's a tradeoff.
[07:55] Sara: what about per-route throttling? we have feature endpoints that are more sensitive to rate limit errors.
[08:01] Marcus: you can set per-route quotas and retries in the client or at the gateway; we also offer automatic client-side backoff and server-side bursts for dedicated.
[08:15] Dmitri: network egress considerations for private on-prem \u0014 do you need outbound to redwood for control?
[08:22] Lena: private can be fully air-gapped if desired, otherwise the control plane needs limited outbound for billing/updates; we can discuss an offline-update cadence.
[08:35] Priya: ok next steps?
[08:38] Lena: recap \u0014 we'll send pricing/security docs, langchain/llamaindex samples, and schedule a Marcus/Dmitri benchmark. action items listed in the follow up.
[08:50] Sara: thanks, this was helpful.
[08:53] Priya: thanks everyone.
[08:55] Marcus: thanks, we'll follow up.
[09:00] [call ends]

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and minor speech-to-text errors (K-V cash -> KV cache, Sasha misattributed).
